Estates and plots

What it is

Every other record points back to a plot. A harvest names the plots it was picked from; a run takes its cherry from harvests; a green lot comes from a run. Add the estate and its plots once, and every bag can be traced back to the ground it grew on.

Also inOne coffee, one chainGetting set up

Step 1 · Open my estates and plots

Open Origin and the Farm tab. Your estates come first, then your plots, each with its variety, area and age. + Estate and + Plot add new ones.

Try it in the app ›

Also inFinding your way

Step 2 · Add my estate

Tap + Estate. Only the Estate name * is needed; add the Village / locality, District, State / region, Country and Total area if you like. Further down, the producer's Postal address, Phone and Email are what a European buyer asks for. Tap Save.

Try it in the app ›

Also inGetting set upOne coffee, one chain

Step 3 · Add a plot

Tap + Plot. Pick the estate, give a Block if you use them, and a Plot name / code * such as U1. Save, then open the plot again to fill in the rest at your own pace.

Also inGetting set upOne coffee, one chain

What it is

An open plot shows a short summary (variety, species, area, last harvest) and buttons that jump to each part: Location, Land check, Plants, Soil, Flowering, Plot and cup, Map, Rows and Photos. Below them, the chain: the harvests picked here, and what came of them.

Also inFinding your wayOne coffee, one chain

Where it is

Step 4 · Put a plot on the map

Stand in the plot and tap Use my location. The latitude and longitude fill in, with how sure the phone is (in metres). For the exact shape, tap Mark outline on map: chapter "Map" below shows how.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Watch out

A plot of 4 hectares or more needs its outline, not only a point: the plot says so in red. Buyers in Europe ask for the outline of large plots.

Also inOne coffee, one chainGuidance, not guarantee

Step 5 · Check a plot against forest maps

With a location or outline saved, tap Run land check. The app compares the plot with the EU's map of forest at the end of 2020 and with tree loss since, and shows the result, the date and the sources. Each check is kept; the newest shows first.

Also inOne coffee, one chainGuidance, not guarantee

Watch out

The land check needs a signal and a signed-in account, and the app says so if either is missing. It is guidance for getting ready, not a certificate. If you change the outline later, the plot says the check describes the earlier shape, and offers Check again.

Also inNothing gets lostGuidance, not guarantee

What grows there

Step 6 · Note variety and spacing

Under Plants, pick the Species and type or choose the Variety. The app shows what it knows about that variety, with its sources. Add the Planting year (the age is worked out), Plant count, and the Row spacing and Plant spacing: planting density per acre and hectare is worked out from them.

Try it in the app ›

Also inQuality as you go

Step 7 · Record soil and how I care for it

Under Soil and soil life: the Soil type, the Texture (feel test), and a tick for each care practice you follow, such as mulch kept on the ground or little digging. Count Earthworms per spadeful if you like. Soil test results are rated against Indian Soil Health Card bands, and inputs applied keep their dates.

Also inQuality as you goGuidance, not guarantee

Step 8 · Time backing and fruit drop

Under Flowering, give the Blossom shower date. The app works out when the backing shower is due (15 to 20 days after) and when fruit drop peaks (90 to 120 days after flowering), from CCRI figures. Add each flowering with + Add flowering.

Also inQuality as you goGuidance, not guarantee

What it is

Plot and cup gathers the cup scores of green lots and roasts made from this plot, beside your other plots. Over seasons it shows which plots and practices give better cups.

Also inQuality as you goOne coffee, one chain

Map, trails and rows

Step 9 · Mark an area on the map

Open Map. Mark an area lets you tap each corner of a plot, then finish; area and height are worked out. Walk the edge records the outline as you walk it. Add a spot marks a store, a drying yard, a house or a water source. Measure gives a distance. Save and share as a GeoJSON file, a KML file (Google Earth) or a printed sheet.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Tip

With no signal the satellite picture cannot load, but points, outlines and the scale still work; the map says so. Your marks are kept on the phone.

Also inNothing gets lost

Step 10 · Walk and record a trail

Open Trails and tap ● Start a trail. Allow location, pick what the trail is (a path, a road, a drain, a boundary, the rows of plants), and walk. Add a photo or a stop with a note on the way. Finish when you are done: distance, time and climb show.

Try it in the app ›

Also inNothing gets lostOne coffee, one chain

Watch out

Keep the screen on and the page open while you walk: phones stop giving the location to a web page when the screen goes off. Trails stay on this phone only, not in your account, so save a backup from the Trails list now and then.

Also inNothing gets lost

Step 11 · Map the rows and number the plants

Open Rows and pick the plot. Add a row in any of four ways:

  • ✏️ Draw a row on the map
  • 🚶 Walk a row with the phone
  • 📍 Row ends (GPS)
  • 〰️ From a trail walked up and down the rows

Give the spacing, and each plant gets a number and a label such as R3-12. Tap a plant to mark it healthy, weak, sick, dead, a gap or replanted.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Step 12 · Compare two ways of caring for plants

On Rows, tap Trials, then ＋ New trial. Name it, choose the block and write your aim. A trial has groups: a Control (left as it is) and one or more Treatments (what you change). Tap ＋ Add a group for more. On each visit you note what you see, and the page shows the groups side by side, with how many plants each figure comes from.

Try it in the app ›

Also inQuality as you go

Watch out

Rust is counted on 4 marked branches per plant, and berries on the number you choose under Berry branches marked per plant. Use the same branches on every visit, or the counts cannot be compared.

Also inQuality as you goRecords you can trust

Care, field log and weather

Step 13 · Read how to grow and pick

Crop care gathers tips on plant health, flowering, fruit set, berry borer and harvest, for Arabica, Robusta or Both, at Basic, Intermediate or Advanced level. Each tip names its source, mostly the Coffee Board and CCRI.

Try it in the app ›

Also inGuidance, not guaranteeQuality as you go

Step 14 · See the year's work, month by month

On Crop care, scroll to Year calendar and open Arabica year or Robusta year. Each is a calendar from the Coffee Board's research institute (CCRI). It lists the work for each part of the year, such as harvest and processing in December to January and manuring before the monsoon in April to May.

Try it in the app ›

Also inGuidance, not guaranteeQuality as you go

Step 15 · Look up a coffee variety or a word

On Origin, tap Coffee varieties and words. Type a name in the search box, or filter the list by All, Arabica, Robusta, Liberica or Excelsa. The India (CCRI) group lists the selections grown in India. Words explained gives the plain meaning of the terms the app uses.

Try it in the app ›

Also inGuidance, not guaranteeFinding your way

Step 16 · Log fertiliser, water and work

Open Field log (an account is needed). Pick the tab: Nutrients, Water, Plant health or Work done, then ＋ New entry. Choose the place and date and fill what you know. For fertiliser, the grade gives the nutrients per hectare.

Try it in the app ›

Also inNothing gets lostRecords you can trust

Step 17 · Keep the weather for my plots

Open Weather (an account is needed) and choose a place. Places come from estates and plots with a GPS point. The app fetches daily rain and temperature from a free weather service and tops it up every night; your own rain gauge can be added as a place without GPS.

Try it in the app ›

Also inQuality as you go

What it is

Field log and Weather, like Team, Jobs, Sales and money, and Land and dues, keep their records in your account, so every phone you sign in on sees the same list. Entries made with no signal wait on the phone and are sent when it is back online; Team, Jobs and Land and dues mark them waiting to send until then.
